units.en: Since the Three, every age has had systems of taxation.
units.literal: since then, all have had methods of taxation.

units.zh: 雖輕重不同，而濟用一也。
units.en: Though the burdens differ in weight, the purpose of meeting public needs is the same.
units.literal: Though light and heavy differ, the purpose of supplying needs is one.

units.zh: 今逆寇未平，軍用資廣，雖未遑減省，以恤民瘼，然令平均，使下無匱。
units.en: Today the rebels are not yet subdued and military costs are heavy; though we cannot yet cut levies to ease the people's distress, we must still distribute burdens evenly so that none below are ruined.
units.literal: Today the rebel enemy is not yet pacified and military expenses are vast; though there is not yet leisure to reduce and economize to relieve the people's distress, still order equal distribution so that those below are not exhausted.

units.zh: 夫平均者，不舍豪強而征貧弱，不縱姦巧而困愚拙，此之謂均也。
units.en: Equal distribution means not exempting the powerful while taxing the weak, nor favoring the cunning while crushing the simple—that is what equality means.
units.literal: Equal distribution means not sparing the powerful and strong while taxing the poor and weak, and not indulging the cunning while burdening the simple and dull—this is called equal.

units.zh: 故聖人曰：「蓋均無貧。」
units.en: As the sage said: "When all is equal, none are poor."
units.literal: Therefore the sage said: "When all is equal, none are poor."

units.zh: 然財貨之生，其功不易。
units.en: Yet wealth is not easily produced.
units.literal: Yet the production of wealth and goods is not easily achieved.

units.zh: 織紝紡績，起於有漸，非旬日之間，所可造次。
units.en: Weaving and spinning build up by degrees and cannot be produced in a few days.
units.literal: Weaving and spinning begin gradually and cannot be hurried in a matter of days.

units.zh: 必須勸課，使預營理。
units.en: Officials must encourage and supervise people so that they prepare in advance.
units.literal: One must encourage and supervise, making people prepare in advance.

units.zh: 絹鄉先事織紝，麻土早脩紡績。
units.en: In silk districts let weaving begin early; in hemp districts let spinning be prepared ahead of time.
units.literal: In silk districts let weaving come first; in hemp districts let spinning be readied early.

units.zh: 先時而備，至時而輸，故王賦獲供，下民無困。
units.en: Prepared in advance and delivered on time, the royal levies are met and the people are not distressed.
units.literal: Prepared beforehand and delivered on time, thus the royal levies are supplied and the people below are not distressed.

units.zh: 如其不預勸戒，臨時迫切，複恐稽緩，以為己過，捶扑交至，取辦目前。
units.en: Without advance warning, officials panic at the deadline, fear delay as their own fault, and resort to beatings to force immediate payment.
units.literal: If there is no advance encouragement and warning, and at the deadline urgency presses, again fearing delay and taking it as one's own fault, beatings come one after another to get results at once.

units.zh: 富商大賈，緣茲射利，有者從之貴買，無者與之舉息。
units.en: Great merchants seize the chance for profit, selling dear to those with money and lending at interest to those without.
units.literal: Great merchants and traders, seizing this chance for profit, sell dear to those who have money and lend at interest to those who have none.

units.zh: 輸稅之民，於是弊矣。
units.en: The tax-paying people are ruined by it.
units.literal: The people who pay taxes are thereby ruined.

units.zh: 在官歲餘，太祖未深知之。
units.en: Su Chuo had been in office for more than a year, and Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai did not yet know him deeply.
units.literal: After more than a year in office, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai did not yet know him deeply.

units.zh: 然諸曹疑事，皆詢於綽而後定。
units.en: Yet whenever a bureau faced a doubtful matter, it consulted Su Chuo before acting.
units.literal: Yet for doubtful matters in the various bureaus, all consulted Su Chuo before deciding.

units.zh: 所行公文，綽又為之條式。
units.en: He also standardized the forms for all outgoing official documents.
units.literal: For official documents issued, Su Chuo also set up formulas for them.

units.zh: 乃召綽，告以其事，綽即為量定。
units.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai summoned Su Chuo, explained the issue, and Su Chuo settled it at once.
units.literal: He then summoned Su Chuo, told him the matter, and Su Chuo immediately weighed and decided it.

units.zh: 惠達以綽對，因稱其有王佐之才。
units.en: Huida named Su Chuo and praised him as a man with the talent to assist a ruler.
units.literal: Huida answered with Su Chuo's name and thereby praised him as having talent to assist a king.

units.zh: 乃與綽並馬徐行至池，竟不設網罟而還。
units.en: He rode beside Su Chuo at an easy pace to the pool, then turned back without ever casting a net.
units.literal: He then rode side by side with Su Chuo at an easy pace to the pool; in the end they set no nets or weirs and returned.

units.zh: 詰朝，謂周惠達曰：「蘇綽真奇士也，吾方任之以政。」
units.en: The next morning he told Zhou Huida: "Su Chuo is a rare talent. I mean to put him in charge of government."
units.literal: At dawn the next day, he said to Zhou Huida: "Su Chuo is truly an extraordinary man; I am about to entrust him with governance."

units.zh: 其先曰托跋思恭，唐僖宗時，為夏、綏、銀、宥節度使，與李茂貞、李克用等破黃巢，複京師，賜姓李氏。
units.en: His forebear Tuoba Sigong served under Emperor Xizong of Tang as military commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You. Together with Li Maozhen, Li Keyong, and others he routed Huang Chao, restored the capital, and received the imperial surname Li.
units.literal: His ancestor was called Tuoba Sigong; in the time of Emperor Xizong of Tang he was military commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You, and with Li Maozhen, Li Keyong, and others defeated Huang Chao, recovered the capital, and was granted the surname Li.

units.zh: 因謂牛弘曰：「崔祖浚所謂問一知二。」
units.en: Thereupon he said to Niu Hong: 'This is what Cui Zujun means by asking one and knowing two.'
units.literal: Thereupon he said to Niu Hong: 'This is what Cui Zujun means by asking one and knowing two.'

units.zh: 掞就宮門階石上裂紙，以唾濡墨，奏言：「臣伏見宋仁宗為一代賢君，而晚年立儲猶豫，其時名臣如范鎮、包拯等，皆交章切諫，鬚髮為白。
units.en: On the palace steps Shan tore paper and wrote with saliva for ink. He said: "I observe that Song Renzong was a sage ruler, yet even he hesitated over the heir in his later years. Ministers such as Fan Zhen and Bao Zheng remonstrated in urgent memorial after memorial until their hair turned white.
units.literal: Shan tore paper on the palace gate steps, moistened ink with saliva, and memorialized: "Your servant has observed that Emperor Renzong of Song was an exemplary ruler of his age, yet in his later years he hesitated over establishing an heir; eminent ministers such as Fan Zhen and Bao Zheng all submitted urgent joint remonstrances until their hair turned white.
